question: Under which strata do trees fall?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Top vertical**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Trees inhabit **the** uppermost vertical layer** of a forest, known as the** canopy**. The arrangement of various species across different levels within this layer is termed stratification.
 
• At the highest level are the emergent trees, followed by the canopy trees forming a continuous layer. Beneath them lie the sub-canopy and understorey tree strata.
 
• Near the forest floor, one may find shrubs, herbs, and grasses.
 
• The tree stratum primarily consists of tall trees, characterized by single-stemmed woody plants that typically exceed 5 meters in height or more upon reaching maturity under favorable growth conditions.
 
• Trees naturally fall when they are unable to sustain themselves in an upright position due to factors such as infestation by insects or diseases.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The vertical distribution **of different species occupying different levels in a forest is termed stratification. For instance, trees typically occupy the topmost vertical strata or layer, followed by shrubs in the middle layer, and herbs and grasses in the bottom layers. The second layer of a forest, known as the understory, comprises small trees, shrubs, vines, and bushes.
 
• In a forest, the** middle layer **primarily consists of shrubs.
 
• **The bottom layer **of a forest, also known as the understory, is characterized by the presence of herbs and shrubs.
